about: Wear OS Compose guidance that is not Material-specific: text input and sign-in through the Wear APIs, rotary scrolling, proportional margins on round screens. Include it after compose-ui: it replaces compose-ui's compose.sign-in.credential-manager and compose.input.keyboard-options with the Wear versions. Each rule quotes developer.android.com and links it.

rules.guidance: Credential Manager is the recommended API for authentication on Wear OS. … There are two other acceptable authentication methods for Wear OS apps: OAuth 2.0 (either variant), and Mobile Auth Token Data Layer Sharing.
rules.check: If the screen signs the user in, does it use the Wear OS methods — Credential Manager (passkeys first, through CredentialManager.getCredential), OAuth 2.0 (PKCE with RemoteAuthClient, or the Device Authorization Grant opening the verification page on the phone with RemoteActivityHelper), or a token the phone app shares over the Data Layer — or Horologist's auth-composables-material3 screens built on them, rather than a hand-built username and password form typed on the watch? Judge from the source and the screen. Answer not_applicable when the screen does not sign anyone in.

rules.guidance: Wear OS users can choose between various input options from Remote Input. … RemoteInput and Wear OS apps expect only single-line text entry.
rules.check: Does the screen take any text through the system's remote input — RemoteInput launched with androidx.wear.input's RemoteInputIntentHelper, which offers dictation, emoji, canned and smart replies and the keyboard — or through speech recognition (RecognizerIntent), rather than drawing its own on-screen keyboard or editable multi-line text fields on the watch? Answer not_applicable when the screen takes no text; a button or chip that opens remote input passes.

rules.guidance: Help people complete tasks on the watch within seconds to avoid ergonomic discomfort or arm fatigue. … Support speech-to-text, because it's much faster on a watch.
rules.check: Does the screen keep typed input to a single short entry, offering choices, voice, or continuing on the phone (RemoteActivityHelper from androidx.wear:wear-remote-interactions) for anything longer, rather than a form of several text fields to fill in on the watch? Answer not_applicable when the screen asks for no text.

rules.guidance: Offer at least one secondary option to handle users dismissing Credential Manager. Provide at least two distinct sign-in options in total.
rules.check: If the screen is where the user chooses how to sign in, does it offer at least two distinct ways (for example Credential Manager and an OAuth or phone hand-off option), rather than a single one such as only "Sign in on phone"? Answer not_applicable when the screen is not a sign-in choice.

rules.guidance: Don't require authentication for all functionality. Instead, provide as many features as possible to the user without requiring them to sign in.
rules.check: If the screen asks the user to sign in, is that tied to an action that needs an account, or does it offer a way to skip or continue as a guest, rather than a sign-in wall in front of everything? Answer not_applicable when the screen does not ask the user to sign in.

rules.guidance: Though expected behavior may vary based on the type of input, be sure to support rotary input for all essential interactions.
rules.check: Judge from the source. Does every scrolling list respond to rotary input — a ScalingLazyColumn, TransformingLazyColumn or Picker inside AppScaffold and ScreenScaffold with its state passed to the ScreenScaffold, or Modifier.rotaryScrollable — rather than a plain Column with verticalScroll or a LazyColumn with no rotary handling? Answer not_applicable when nothing scrolls.

rules.guidance: All top, bottom, and side margins should be defined in percentages to avoid clipping and provide proportional scaling of elements.
rules.check: Judge from the source. Are the screen's outer margins proportional to the screen — the scaffold's content padding, rememberResponsiveColumnPadding, or a fraction of the screen size — rather than fixed dp padding on the outermost container, which clips on small round screens and wastes space on large ones? Answer not_applicable when the subject is a component shown on its own.
